newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Jordan warn of dangers of peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Jordan warn of dangers of peace crisis.

text.p: Foreign ministers of Egypt and Jordan said on Thursday it was dangerous to leave the latest Middle East peace crisis unresolved and reiterated Arab concerns over Israeli sanctions against the Palestinians.

The ministers were talking to reporters after Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan met to discuss diplomatic efforts aimed at solving the crisis set off by twin suicide bombings which killed 15 people in Jerusalem last week.
Egypt's Amr Moussa and Jordan's Fayez al-Tarawnah and the Arab League welcomed a possible visit to the region by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright as a positive step.
"The danger of the present situation is its continuation. Egypt and Jordan are coordinating on how to salvage the peace process which is being threatened with so many challenges," Moussa said.
Egypt and Jordan, the only two Arab states which have peace deals with Israel, have led efforts to ease the latest crisis ahead of a visit to the region by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross.
In the aftermath of the bombing, the deadliest attack against Israelis in a year, Israel suspended a resumption of its talks with the Palestinians and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Palestinians have described the measures as collective punishment and have gathered Arab backing for their calls on Israel to lift the sanctions.

"Collective punishment must end immediately. We don't need anymore negative signs...From the same logic with which we reject violence that leads to the death of innocents, so we also reject the sanctions against the Palestinians," Moussa said.
Prince Hassan failed in talks with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Wednesday to persuade Israel to end the sanctions.
Netanyahu said Israel would ease the measures only after the Palestinian Authority begins to fight "terrorism".

An Egyptian government newspaper said on Thursday Israel must lift sanctions against Palestinians before the leaders of Egypt, Israel and the Palestinians could hold a summit to ease the latest Middle East peace crisis.

Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah said in Alexandria: "There is still a big gap between the Palestinians and the Israelis, not only in security issues but also in political issues and those which have to do with negotiations.
"There are encouraging and positive signs regarding the intention of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to visit the region after a long absence," Tarawnah said.
Albright said on Wednesday she would travel to the region at the end of August provided progress was made in security there.
Moussa welcomed comments by Albright that called on Israel and the Palestinians to avoid unilateral measures and work as partners for peace.

"Madeleine Albright articulated a certain new American position concerning the peace process...On the Palestinian-Israeli track she was very clear that in addition to security, important as it is, it is equally important that no unilateral measures be undertaken because those measures undermine the future of the peace process."

Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid said in a statement on Thursday he hoped Albright's planned visit "would lead to serious reactivation of the peace process so as to defuse the current situation in the region on the way to achieving a just, comprehensive and permanent peace for all the people of the region".
